mainTopic: Choosing a trade, where פרנסה comes from, and why תורה lasts a lifetime
overview: This amud finishes explaining the משנה's advice about teaching a son a trade, and it brings מסכת קידושין to a close. First, the גמרא gives fine embroidery needlework as an example of a clean, easy trade. Then רבי teaches in a ברייתא that the world needs every trade, but it is better to have a pleasant one. רבי מאיר adds that a person should teach his son a clean trade and pray, because wealth comes from ה׳, not from the job. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר uses a קל וחומר: animals get their food without struggle, so people should too. People struggle only because of their sins. Last, רבי נהוראי says he teaches his son only תורה, because a trade helps only in youth, while תורה helps in youth and gives hope in old age. He proves this with two פסוקים. The amud ends with the הדרן for פרק עשרה יוחסין and the end of מסכת קידושין.

steps.title: Example of a clean and easy trade
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives an example of the משנה's 'clean and easy trade': fine embroidery needlework.
steps.simpleTranslation: A clean and easy trade is needlework for embroidery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a question asked just before: what is the 'clean and easy trade' the משנה recommends? The answer is embroidery needlework.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה told a father to teach his son a trade that is clean and easy, but it did not give an example. This line gives a concrete one: fine needlework is not dirty and does not need heavy labor.

phrases.english: Needlework for embroidery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question (asked just before) defining the משנה's 'clean and easy trade'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is an example of a clean and easy trade?

steps.title: Every trade is needed, but some are better
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that the world needs every trade, yet it is a blessing to have a pleasant one. He compares this to the perfumer and the tanner, and to sons and daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: No trade will ever disappear from the world. Still, fortunate is the one whose parents work in a fine trade, and woe to the one whose parents work in a lowly trade. The world cannot exist without perfumers or without tanners. But fortunate is the perfumer, and woe to the tanner. The world cannot exist without males or without females. But fortunate is one whose children are sons, and woe to one whose children are daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי says that every trade is necessary, but some are more pleasant to have. He gives three pairs to show the idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי makes the same point three times. Something can be necessary for the world and still be harder or less pleasant for the person involved. The tanner is just as needed as the perfumer, but his work smells bad. This adds to the משנה's advice: pick the better trade if you can.

keyTerms.meaning: A tanner, who works with smelly hides

phrases.english: It is taught: Rebbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ אוּמָּנוּת שֶׁעוֹבֶרֶת מִן הָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: There is no trade that passes away from the world.
Fortunate is one who sees his parents
in a fine trade;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹי לוֹ לְמִי שֶׁרוֹאֶה אֶת הוֹרָיו
phrases.english: woe to one who sees his parents
in a lowly trade.
It is impossible for the world
to be without a perfumer and without a tanner.
Fortunate is one whose trade is perfume,
and woe to one whose trade is tanning.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added by the corrected wording, so read it as 'to one whose'.

phrases.english: It is impossible for the world
to be without males and without females;
fortunate is one whose children are males,
and woe to one whose children are females.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵין לְךָ אוּמָּנוּת שֶׁעוֹבֶרֶת מִן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that supports choosing a pleasant trade, while saying that all trades are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every trade is necessary for the world, but it is better to have a pleasant one.

steps.title: Wealth comes from ה׳, not from the trade
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר advises teaching a son a clean, easy trade and praying to ה׳. Rich or poor depends on ה׳, not on the job.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: A person should always teach his son a clean and easy trade, and pray for mercy to the One Who owns all wealth and property. Poverty does not come from a trade, and riches do not come from a trade. They come from the One Who owns wealth, as the פסוק says: 'Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold, says ה׳ of hosts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי מאיר, who adds that besides choosing a good trade, a person must pray. Money comes from ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why רבי מאיר can recommend an easy trade instead of the most profitable one. If income really depended on the job, you would choose the job that pays most. Since wealth comes from ה׳, the job only needs to be decent, and prayer is what matters.

keyTerms.meaning: And he should ask for mercy, pray

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic idea about פרנסה: a person must make an effort, but the result comes from ה׳.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
A person should always teach his son
a clean and easy trade,
and he should ask for mercy
from the One to Whom wealth and property belong,
for poverty does not come from the trade,
and wealth does not come from the trade,
rather, from the One to Whom wealth belongs,
as it is said: "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold,
says the Lord of hosts."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם יְלַמֵּד אָדָם לִבְנוֹ אוּמָּנוּת נְקִיָּה וְקַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with רבי מאיר's view, adding prayer and the idea that wealth comes from ה׳.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teach a clean, easy trade and pray, since wealth and poverty come from ה׳, not from the trade.

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר to introduce a ברייתא that explains them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: 'Have you ever in your days seen...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement in the משנה. It is setting up the next step, a ברייתא that gives his full words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה quoted him only briefly. Quoting his opening words points the reader back to the משנה, so the fuller ברייתא can be read as its explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: In your days, ever in your life

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Have you ever in your days seen...

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אִם רָאִיתָ מִיָּמֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new opinion in the משנה, that of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the discussion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement.

steps.title: Animals get food without working
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר observes that animals never work at trades, yet they get their food without pain. He adds that they were made to serve people, and people were made to serve ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: In my life I never saw a deer drying figs, a lion working as a porter, or a fox running a store. Yet they get their food without suffering. They were created only to serve me, and I was created to serve my Maker.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the full words of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. He sets up two facts that his argument in the next step will use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first fact is that animals have no jobs, yet they eat without struggling. The second fact is that animals are on a lower level, since they serve man, while man serves ה׳. Together these facts prepare a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A porter, one who carries loads
Earn a living, get their food

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
In my days I never saw a deer drying figs,
or a lion as a porter, or a fox as a storekeeper,
and yet they earn their living without suffering.
And they were created only to serve me,
and I was created to serve my Maker.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: מִיָּמַי לֹא רָאִיתִי צְבִי קַיָּיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full ברייתא behind the משנה's short quote.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals, created to serve man, eat without suffering; man was created to serve ה׳.

steps.title: The קל וחומר: people should eat without struggle
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר builds a קל וחומר. If lower creatures eat without pain, people, who serve ה׳, surely should too. So why don't they?
steps.simpleTranslation: If these animals, created only to serve me, get their food without suffering, then I, created to serve my Maker, should surely get my food without suffering!
steps.whatsHappening: Using the two facts from the last step, he argues that people should have an easy living. This raises a puzzle, because in real life people do struggle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic goes from a lower creature to a higher one. If the lower one gets food without pain, the higher one surely should. The question is rhetorical: it shows that our real struggle needs an explanation, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lesser case to a greater case
Is it not logical? (a סברא-based conclusion)

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֵלּוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרְאוּ אֶלָּא לְשַׁמְּשֵׁנִי
phrases.english: If these, who were created only to serve me,
earn their living without suffering,
then I, who was created to serve my Maker,
is it not logical that I should earn my living without suffering?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אֵלּוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרְאוּ אֶלָּא לְשַׁמְּשֵׁנִי מִתְפַּרְנְסִים שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two facts from step 5 to build a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reality that people struggle to earn a living.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By קל וחומר from animals, people should eat without suffering, yet they do not.

steps.title: Sin is why people struggle for פרנסה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: people struggle only because their bad deeds caused them to lose their easy livelihood, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I made my deeds bad, and so I lost my livelihood, as the פסוק says: 'Your sins have turned these things away.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר answers his own puzzle. People were supposed to eat without struggle, but their sins took that away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר was correct in principle: man should have an easy living. The gap between that and reality is explained by sin, backed up by a פסוק in ירמיהו.

keyTerms.meaning: I made bad, I did wrong

steps.whatToRemember: Animals eat without struggle, and people should too. People struggle for פרנסה only because of their sins. This fits רבי מאיר's teaching that livelihood comes from ה׳.

phrases.english: But I made my deeds bad
and lost my livelihood,
as it is said: "Your iniquities have turned away."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁהֲרֵעוֹתִי אֶת מַעֲשַׂי וְקִיפַּחְתִּי אֶת פַּרְנָסָתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the puzzle raised by the קל וחומר in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the gap between the expected result and reality with an outside cause: sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By קל וחומר, people should eat without suffering.
steps.terutzMaskana: People would have eaten without suffering, but their sins caused them to lose that.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Human struggle for livelihood comes from sin, not from how the world was meant to be.

steps.title: Quoting רבי נהוראי's words from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of רבי נהוראי from the משנה to set up a ברייתא that explains them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נהוראי says: I set aside all trades, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה, רבי נהוראי's statement. This is a setup line that prepares for the ברייתא coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the גמרא did with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in Step 4, it now points to רבי נהוראי's words in the משנה. The 'וכו׳' means 'and so on', telling us the rest of his words are in the משנה. No new idea is added yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on; the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Rabbi Nehorai says:
I set aside all trades, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of his words in the משנה: 'and I teach my son only Torah.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי אוֹמֵר: מַנִּיחַ אֲנִי כׇּל אוּמָּנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's teaching to the next opinion in the משנה, רבי נהוראי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גמרא points to רבי נהוראי's statement in the משנה as the subject of the next ברייתא.

steps.title: Why רבי נהוראי teaches his son only תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives רבי נהוראי's full words: a trade helps only in youth, but תורה helps in youth and gives hope in old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי נהוראי says, I set aside every trade in the world and teach my son only תורה. Every trade helps a person only while he is young; when he is old, he is left hungry. תורה is different: it helps a person when he is young and gives him a future and hope when he is old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives רבי נהוראי's full statement and his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new information is the reason. A trade depends on physical strength, so it fails a person once he grows old. תורה does not run out with age; it keeps supporting a person all his life.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי נהוראי is not saying a trade is useless. He is saying it only lasts while a person is young and strong, while תורה lasts his whole life.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Nehorai says:
I set aside all the trades in the world

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינִי מְלַמֵּד אֶת בְּנִי אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: and I teach my son only Torah,
because every trade in the world

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹמֶדֶת לוֹ אֶלָּא בִּימֵי יַלְדוּתוֹ,
phrases.english: serves a person only in the days of his youth,
but in the days of his old age
he is left lying in hunger.
But Torah is not like this:
it serves a person in the time of his youth,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹתֶנֶת לוֹ אַחֲרִית וְתִקְוָה בְּעֵת זִקְנוּתוֹ.
phrases.english: and gives him a future and hope in the time of his old age.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full ברייתא version of the משנה line quoted in Step 8, with the reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teach a son only תורה, because a trade helps only in youth, while תורה helps in youth and gives hope in old age.

steps.title: פסוקים showing תורה helps in youth and old age
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים prove each half of the claim: one for youth, one for old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: About youth, what does the פסוק say? 'Those who hope in ה׳ will renew their strength; they will rise up with wings like eagles.' About old age, what does it say? 'They will still bear fruit in old age; they will be full of sap and fresh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings two פסוקים to back up רבי נהוראי's claim about youth and old age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows that people who connect to ה׳ get strength while young. The second shows they stay fruitful and fresh even when old. Together they prove that תורה supports a person through his whole life.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נהוראי, a trade lasts only while a person is strong, but תורה gives strength in youth and fruit and hope in old age.

phrases.english: About the time of his youth, what does it say?
"But those who hope in the Lord shall renew their strength,
they shall rise up with wings like eagles"
About his old age, what does it say?
"They shall still bear fruit in old age,
they shall be full of sap and fresh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports both halves of the claim in Step 9 with פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that תורה supports a person both in youth and in old age.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 40:31 for youth, and תהלים 92:15 for old age.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing עשרה יוחסין and מסכת קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק עשרה יוחסין and for the whole מסכת קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק עשרה יוחסין, and מסכת קידושין is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the הדרן, the traditional line said when finishing a פרק. Here it also marks the end of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן expresses the hope to come back and learn this פרק again. Since עשרה יוחסין is the last פרק, the line adds that מסכת קידושין is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: Name of the last פרק (Ten Lineages)

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת קידושין ends with the message that a person's living comes from ה׳, and that תורה supports a person his whole life.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Asara Yuchasin,
and Tractate Kiddushin is completed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק עשרה יוחסין and all of מסכת קידושין are complete.
